newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tight liquidity forces German call money rates up.
newsitem.headline: Tight liquidity forces German call money rates up.

text.p: German call money rates advanced further beyond the three percent securities repurchase rate on Tuesday as dealers bemoaned a four-billion-mark liquidity squeeze.

Dealers said rates had risen to 3.20 to 3.25 percent, slightly above Monday's levels. The Bundesbank was widely expected to fill the liquidity gap with a four billion mark injection at this week's tender.
Bank deposits with the central bank on Monday dropped to 36.4 billion marks from 37.7 billion while the monthly average eased to 40.1 billion marks from 40.5 billion.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was at 3.24800 (3.18700) percent.
